signatures.signature: pub const SCRATCH_GRACE: Duration; pub fn scan_scratch(scratch: &Path) -> std::io::Result<Vec<ScratchEntry>>; pub fn select_for_cleanup(entries: &[ScratchEntry], live: &HashMap<String, Option<String>>, now: SystemTime, grace: Duration) -> Vec<PathBuf>; pub fn clean_scratch(scratch: &Path, live: &HashMap<String, Option<String>>, now: SystemTime, grace: Duration) -> usize
signatures.doc: snipmd_core::cleanup (ScratchEntry stays in core lib.rs as it is). SCRATCH_GRACE = 14 days. `live` maps the id of every tab in the session (open and closed) to its text when known, None when not (a disk tab: its text is not in the session). scan_scratch: one entry per folder directly in `scratch` whose name passes paths::valid_tab_id (is_dir true, tab_id = its name), and one per item directly inside such a folder (is_dir false, same tab_id); modified from metadata; loose files at the scratch root, other folder names and deeper levels are not listed; an entry whose metadata fails is left out; a missing `scratch` gives Ok(empty). select_for_cleanup (pure): a tab folder is selected when its tab_id is not in `live` and both the folder and every item inside it are at least `grace` old; its items are then not listed separately. An item in a folder whose tab is live with Some(text) is selected when it is at least `grace` old and neither its file name nor links::encode_link_path(file name) occurs in that text (substring match; conservative). An item of a tab with None, or of a non-live folder that is not selected, is kept. A modified time after `now` counts as young. clean_scratch: scan, select, then remove each selected path (remove_dir_all for a folder, remove_file for an item), only when the path starts_with `scratch`; a failure skips that path; returns how many were removed; a scan error removes nothing and returns 0.

signatures.signature: src-tauri/src/lib.rs: startup cleanup inside load_session; no new command
signatures.doc: After load_session has read and parsed session.json, once per process (a static AtomicBool or std::sync::Once), build `live` from session_tabs (open and closed tabs): a string id maps to Some(content, or "" when missing) when filePath is null or missing, to None otherwise; an id seen as None stays None. Then std::thread::spawn a cleanup::clean_scratch(app_data/scratch, live, SystemTime::now(), SCRATCH_GRACE) so startup never waits for it; eprintln the count when it is above 0. No session.json, a read error or JSON that does not parse: no cleanup at all (nothing is known to be unused). Single instance already resolves relative paths against the second launch's cwd (open_args): keep it unchanged.

signatures.signature: src/tabs.ts closeTab(id): Promise<TabState | undefined>; reopenClosed(id?: string): Promise<TabState | undefined>; markSaved also updates a closed entry; src/infobar.ts clearTabInfo(id)
signatures.doc: Already written by the main session (commit 9401e13); read them, do not edit them. closeTab puts the tab at the front of the closed-tabs list (20 entries, 14 days) with its latest text and returns it; it does not save, clear bars or show anything. reopenClosed takes an entry off the list (the newest without id), reopens it with the same id (a clean disk tab is read again) and returns it, or activates the open tab for that note and returns undefined. clearTabInfo removes every bar whose key ends in `:<tab id>`.

signatures.signature: export async function closeTabWithRestore(id: string): Promise<void>; export async function restoreClosedTab(id?: string): Promise<void>
signatures.doc: src/closedTabs.ts, the close and restore commands. closeTabWithRestore: no tab, nothing. A dirty disk tab that is not inConflict gets void saveTab(id) BEFORE closeTab (the write holds the tab object and reads the closed text; a write that ends later marks the entry saved through markSaved). A tab in conflict is not written and keeps its conflict flag while closed, so no queued write overwrites the outside change. Then closeTab(id), then clearTabInfo(id) (its first-save bar ends through its own onClose), then the restore bar: showInfo({kind: 'info', key: 'closed', position: 'bottom', timeoutMs: 8000, text, body, actions: [{label: 'Restore', primary: true, run: () => void restoreClosedTab(id)}]}); text is `<title> closed.` or `<title> closed, with N screenshot(s).` (1 screenshot, N screenshots) where N is the number of distinct relative image URLs in the closed text (Markdown `![alt](url)`, url without a scheme and not starting with `/`); body is a <kbd> with textContent `Ctrl+Shift+T`, built with DOM APIs. A newer close replaces the bar (same key). restoreClosedTab: tab = await reopenClosed(id); when a tab came back, resolveConflict(tab.id) so the external watch compares it with its file again; clearInfo('closed') in every case. An empty list does nothing.

signatures.signature: src/app.ts registerKeys and the titlebar close handler
signatures.doc: The SPEC §10 table, keydown on window with Ctrl (or Meta) and no Alt: Ctrl+T and Ctrl+N newUntitled; Ctrl+O open; Ctrl+S saveTab; Ctrl+Shift+S saveAs; Ctrl+W closeTabWithRestore(active); Ctrl+Shift+T restoreClosedTab(); Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle(1 / -1); Ctrl+1..Ctrl+9 activate the Nth tab of getTabs() when it exists, matched on e.code `Digit1`..`Digit9` and `Numpad1`..`Numpad9` (on AZERTY e.key of Ctrl+1 is `&`); Ctrl+E toggleMode. Every handled key calls preventDefault; Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H (phase 6), Ctrl+V and Ctrl+Shift+V (paste.ts) are not handled here. The titlebar close button and middle-click use closeTabWithRestore. Delete closeAndSave.
